title: Turning down Joe Henderson
summary: Short stints with Herman and Miller; he refused Henderson's bass clarinet job, and recalls Henderson's rock band gear.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well you went from Woody Herman and Buddy Rich and Elvin Jones, were there any gigs that you turned down along the way?

Well I was with Woody Herman only for a short bit, I just went out to help Frank Tiberi and they just called me up as a sub. I loved it, but I wasn’t with them for a long time. Same with the Glenn Miller band. I went out for a bit to help somebody that needed to get off for a week. Yeah, I turned down Joe Henderson believe it or not, I’ll tell you why, because I was studying with Joe Henderson in New York. I was on Buddy Rich’s band. And you know Joe called me one day, I was in a hotel, the President Hotel in New York and he called me and he said, “I need somebody to go on, to play bass clarinet.” He wanted me to play bass clarinet. I said, “Joe, I can’t play bass clarinet.” I think Pete Yellin was doing the gig maybe at the time. I’m not sure if Pete was doing it. But he wanted me to go out and play with the band and he had this idea of bass clarinet and I just said I can’t do it. I’m not a bass clarinet player. I mean I had to play clarinet with Buddy’s band and I started on that instrument, but no way was I going to go out and embarrass myself with Joe Henderson.
He had a big band at the time?

This was the small band. He had like I think it was either Julian Priester, or I think he had three horns in front. I know at one point he had alto, trombone and himself on tenor. I had seen that band at the Vanguard. I don’t know what he was thinking at the time, but he was always composing. When I was with him he was writing for Blood, Sweat & Tears,
when I was studying with him he was kind of doing that Blood, Sweat & Tears band that never took off. They were just rehearsing all the time.
I remember seeing that, like Joe Henderson is with Blood, Sweat & Tears? Because I loved Blood, Sweat & Tears.

I went to take a lesson one time and Joe says, “Look at this,” he said, “I got a complete brand new Magnavox sound system.” He goes, “They gave me a tenor, a bari, an alto, a soprano.” Because Magnavox owned Selmer at the time. He said, “I got all of this stuff they gave me because I joined a rock band. I played jazz all my life nobody ever gave me anything,” he said, “I go with one rock band and look at all the stuff they give me.”
